motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 14.A. and 14.B. and moving them to Scheduled Items. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Two Overland items pulled for separate votes
motions.summary: The council approved its routine consent items in one batch but pulled the two Overland agreements out to be discussed and voted on separately.
motions.impact: This is procedural housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It only meant the two Overland items got their own discussion instead of passing in a batch.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Land Exchange Agreement with SITLA for the Exchange of Properties in the Overland Area.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Land Exchange Agreement with SITLA for the Exchange of Properties in the Overland Area conditioned upon : 1. Reciprocal language be added to Section 8 of the agreement ; and 2. SITLA guarantees clean title of warranty . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Trade land with the state in Overland
motions.summary: The city approved a land exchange with SITLA, the state land agency, in the Overland area, conditioned on reciprocal contract language and a guaranteed clean title.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day. The swap only rearranges who owns which parcels in Overland, and the motion says nothing about what will be built there.

motions.headline: Agreement signed on the Overland area

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Portion of Utah Cou nty Parcel #46:489:0159 of Designated “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal : 1. motions.headline: Sell city land at $2.07 a square foot
motions.summary: The city approved selling part of a county parcel at $2.07 per square foot, with the total set by the final survey and existing utility easements kept in place.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan , directing consultant to take feedback presented and return with revisions at a future work session , along with an agenda item for potential approval at the same meeting
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan , directing consultant to take feedback presented and return with revisions at a future work session , along with an agenda item for potential approval at the same meeting. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Parks and trails plan sent back for revisions
motions.summary: The council delayed adopting the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan and told its consultant to revise it using the feedback given and bring it back.
motions.impact: No decision yet on the city's long-range plan for parks, trails and open space. It returns at a future work session before any vote.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City , Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15 regarding Noise to Modify Maximum Decibel Levels During Hours of Restriction as presented by staff , with the change that morning hours be adjusted from 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., seven day a week
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City , Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15 regarding Noise to Modify Maximum Decibel Levels During Hours of Restriction as presented by staff , with the change that morning hours be adjusted from 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., seven day a week. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Noise limits now lift at 7 a.m., not 9 a.m.
motions.summary: The city rewrote its noise rules, ending the morning restriction at 7 a.m. instead of 9 a.m., seven days a week, and changing the decibel limits during restricted hours.
motions.impact: Loud activity can legally start two hours earlier every morning, weekends included. If noise near your home wakes you, expect it to be allowed from 7 a.m.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 2.35 (Public Library) and Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.15 (Roles and Duties) to Eagle Mountain City CouMnicnilu te –s April 7, 2026 Page9 of 12 Modify the Timing of Appointments from January 1 – December 31 to April 1 – March 31
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 2.35 (Public Library) and Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.15 (Roles and Duties) to Eagle Mountain City CouMnicnilu te –s April 7, 2026 Page9 of 12 Modify the Timing of Appointments from January 1 – December 31 to April 1 – March 31. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Shift board terms to an April–March year
motions.summary: The city changed its code so appointments to the library board and other city boards run April 1 through March 31 instead of January through December.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping. It only affects people who serve on city boards, and nothing changes for other residents.

motions.item_title: Add pursuing a Justice Court with Utah County be added to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add pursuing a Justice Court with Utah County be added to the Legislative Priorities List . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Pursue a justice court with Utah County
motions.summary: The council added pursuing a justice court with Utah County to its Legislative Priorities List.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for you now — this only puts the idea on the city's priority list. Any actual court would take separate decisions later.

motions.item_title: Add a temporary business signage provision to the Legislative Priorities List, with direction f…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to add a temporary business signage provision to the Legislative Priorities List, with direction for staff to return with a proposal to the City Council. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Take up rules for temporary business signs
motions.summary: The council added a temporary business signage provision to its Legislative Priorities List and asked staff to come back with an actual proposal.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet. If you run a business here, the rules for putting up temporary signs could change once staff bring a proposal back to the council.
